summary: This paper concatenates quantum Reed–Solomon codes with large-alphabet Galois qudits ($q = 2048$) as outer codes over the 144-qubit gross bivariate bicycle code as inner code, reaching the teraquop regime (logical error rates $10^{-14}$–$10^{-13}$ per logical qubit-round) at uniform physical noise $p = 10^{-3}$ with lower space overhead than the 288-qubit two-gross code down to $4.1 \times 10^{-15}$ per logical qubit-round. The construction introduces spacetime error mixing to handle unknown logical error distributions of the inner code and demonstrates fault-tolerant syndrome extraction via Galois qudit Shor schemes with time-like Reed–Solomon codes protecting measurement errors.
motivation: High-rate quantum LDPC codes like the gross code reduce space overhead compared to surface codes but require non-local connectivity; concatenation with outer codes relaxes this trade-off, enables modular architectures, and allows recovery from localized catastrophic errors.
method: The 11 non-pivot logical qubits of each gross code are packaged into a single $q=2^{11}$-dimensional Galois qudit, enabling concatenation with quantum Reed–Solomon outer codes of parameters $[[n, n-2(d-1), d]]_q$. Fault-tolerant syndrome extraction uses qudit cat states prepared via repeated fault-tolerant measurements of weight-two stabilizers, with overcomplete syndrome bases protected by time-like Reed–Solomon codes. Spacetime error mixing averages over random qudit-to-qubit basis choices and linear combination parameters to bound failure probabilities using only aggregate inner-code statistics.
result: At $p=10^{-3}$, the concatenated gross code achieves $\sim 4.1 \times 10^{-15}$ logical error rate per logical qubit-round with $<500\,000$ physical qubits and better space overhead than the 288-qubit two-gross code; list decoding of large-alphabet Reed–Solomon codes suppresses weight-3 and weight-4 error rates by factors $\sim n(d-M)/(q-1)^M$, a genuine advantage absent for qubits ($q=2$).
